title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: Preregistered Evaluation of Input Sanitization and Deterministic Verification
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within an orchestration adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.74468085106383%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording vs the formal estimand, document pipeline semantics and shared_initial_candidate reuse, disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts (execution manifest [14]).

sections.introduction:
Large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to translate operator intent into device CLI to accelerate network operations (NetOps). While automation promises operational efficiency, generated configurations can violate ordering constraints, CLI grammar, or safety invariants; adversarially manipulated inputs can exacerbate these risks. Deterministic validators that operate on concrete configuration semantics (rather than token overlap) are a natural deployment gate, yet published evaluations commonly report string-based metrics that do not directly measure validator acceptance or deployability [3,8,9].

This study asks a narrowly scoped, operational question that can be addressed with preregistered inference: Under a shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, does template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair change the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? We executed the preregistered study cand-2026-03 end-to-end with artifact-backed analysis to estimate the paired difference in validator-accepted outcomes between the guarded pipeline (sanitization + verifier-gating ± repair) and baseline (validator applied to the shared initial draft). Our execution artifacts and analysis are archived and cited (execution manifest [14]).
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-verification tools provide semantics-focused checks and have been applied as deployment gates because they report property-level violations (reachability, isolation, sequencing) rather than syntactic mismatches. Classic systems such as Header Space Analysis and VeriFlow illustrate this representational difference and the operational appeal of validator-centered gating, while also highlighting that validators require explicit formalization of intended invariants and do not automatically cover all dynamic or protocol-level properties [5–7,14].

Empirical NetOps work studying LLM-assisted configuration (e.g., NetConfEval, NetLLMBench) consistently finds that model-only generation yields both syntactic and higher-level semantic errors — ordering mistakes, precondition violations, and policy breaches — and that surface metrics (BLEU, token-match) correlate poorly with deployability [3,8,9]. Prototype generate–validate–repair architectures, where an LLM produces a candidate, a verifier checks it, and feedback is converted into constrained repairs, have shown promise for improving concrete outcome metrics on narrow tasks when verifier diagnostics are precise and repair scope is bounded [11,3,32].

Security analyses identify prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks as practical threats to LLM-integrated systems; these motivate defenses such as template-based input sanitization, slot validation, and deterministic gating that programmatically block verifier-failing candidates [10,43]. Prior surveys and benchmarks emphasize fragmented evaluation practices and call for operationally meaningful, validator-centered metrics; our work responds to that gap by preregistering validator acceptance as the primary estimand and by executing a paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate downstream pipeline effects [4,9].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to outcome observation (preregistration archived; execution manifest [14]). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent, define a binary outcome equal to 1 if the deterministic validator accepts the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes. Bootstrap percentile 95% CIs were computed with 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729.

Design, task bank, and adversary. The design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents (paired Baseline vs Guarded). The synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN updates, constrained required sequences (shutdown–change–restore), and protected-interface rules. The adversary model applied deterministic mutation heuristics to templates; task-generation seeds and mutation taxonomy are archived in the execution manifest. Scope is intentionally synthetic and limited to the CLI grammar and invariants encoded in our validator.

Model, validator, orchestration, and protocol deviation. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration used a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter implementing the guarded pipeline. The guarded branch applied template-based sanitization prior to gating; the sanitizer and gating policy are described in archived task payloads (execution manifest [14]). The archived model configuration records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and an unset temperature field (temperature = null). We disclose the unset temperature as a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults can affect sampling; to preserve paired comparability the run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generation per pair).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and pipeline timeline. Because generation semantics were registered as shared_initial_candidate, each paired unit followed: (1) task instantiation and adversarial mutation; (2) a single LLM call produced the shared_initial_candidate used by both conditions; (3) Baseline scoring: deterministic validator applied to the shared draft; (4) Guarded branch: sanitizer applied and, if allowed by policy, at-most-one automated repair LLM call permitted; (5) final validation of the sanitized or repaired candidate. This preregistered semantics ensures the paired comparison isolates downstream guarded-pipeline effects (sanitization, gating, and bounded repair) rather than differences in initial generation.

Missingness, exclusions, and analysis executor. The preregistered missingness plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. The archive reports completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs_included = 141. Primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (exact McNemar) and the published bootstrap parameters (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Secondary and sensitivity analyses followed the preregistered plan archived with the execution manifest [14].
sections.results:
Execution summary and provider-call accounting. The run completed 282 of 300 planned episodes; 18 episodes failed for technical reasons recorded per the preregistered missingness rules. After applying the exclusion rule (exclude a paired unit only when both paired runs are technical failures) 141 complete pairs entered the primary analysis. Provider-call accounting in the reconciliation artifact reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed = 147, failed = 9; stage counts report 150 shared_initial_generation events and 6 repair-stage events.

Condition-level outcomes and paired contingency. Condition summaries: baseline_successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085106383) and guarded_successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency table observed n11 = 135 (both accepted), n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0 (baseline accepted, guarded rejected), n00 = 0 (both rejected). The observed paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165.

Confirmatory inference and CI. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar yields p = 0.03125. The 95% bootstrap percentile confidence interval for the paired difference was computed with 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) and is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. These numeric results and analysis parameters are reproducible from the archived analysis artifacts cited in the execution manifest [14].

Discordant-case diagnostics. The six n10 discordant pairs are traceable in the archived per-episode validator traces. Reconciliation links repair-stage activity to these discordant pairs: the repair-stage count equals six, and each discordant pair shows sanitizer normalization and/or a single permitted repair converted a draft the baseline validator would reject into a final candidate the validator accepted. Detailed per-episode traces are retained in the archive ([14]).

Sensitivity to technical failures. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically. As a conservative post-hoc sensitivity check (not the preregistered primary analysis), treating those excluded pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; this conservative assumption reduces effective sample size but does not invert the observed paired difference under this scenario.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the formal estimand versus attacker-centric claims. The preregistration natural-language H1 stated that verifier-gating would reduce attacker success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand measured paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These differ: an increase in validator acceptance can indicate successful repair of reparable but benign drafts rather than reduced attacker success. In our run the guarded pipeline produced higher acceptance (≈4.255 percentage points) because sanitizer and bounded repair recovered reparable drafts the baseline validator rejected. Therefore the preregistered directional claim about reducing attacker success is not supported if ‘‘attacker success’’ is interpreted as undetected malicious semantic changes; to measure attacker-centric safety requires an independent semantic-safety oracle coupled to validator acceptance (a recommendation we preregistered).

Operational implications and co-design trade-offs. Within this synthetic scope, input sanitization plus bounded automated repair can reduce operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates. The six discordant cases illustrate this benefit: each required sanitizer normalization or a single automated repair to pass the validator. However, repairs that enable acceptance introduce risk if repair semantics diverge from operator intent or mask adversarial manipulations. Operational deployment therefore requires co-design: (i) explicitly specify validator coverage (which semantics are checked), (ii) bound repair scope and transparency (logs, diffs, and human approval thresholds), and (iii) define escalation policies for repairs that materially change required sequence structure.

Threats to validity and generality. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size and were handled per the preregistered exclusion rule. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes CLI grammar, required sequences, and protected-interface invariants but does not represent all protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics; therefore acceptance-for-deployment is a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: a single generator (gpt-5-mini), a single validator, and a synthetic intent bank limit generalization across vendors, CLI dialects, and production traffic. Conclusion validity: the absolute effect is small against a high baseline (ceiling effect); statistical significance at alpha=0.05 (p = 0.03125) signals detectability but not necessarily substantial operational impact across broader settings.

Reproducibility guidance and the disclosed protocol deviation. The archived model configuration recorded temperature = null (unset); this is disclosed because provider-side defaults can affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics and the reconciliation artifacts record provider-call accounting. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 and re-executing the archived execution manifest; the manifest and analysis artifacts contain the complete run record and parameters necessary for reproduction (execution manifest [14]).

Recommendations. (1) Execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; (2) preregister and measure an attacker-centric estimand that couples validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle or reachability tests; (3) diversify generators and validators across vendors and CLI dialects; (4) fix sampling settings (temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction; and (5) treat automated repairs as visible, auditable transformations with conservative scope and human-in-the-loop escalation thresholds.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank to evaluate whether template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair changes deterministic-validator acceptance of LLM-generated configurations under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On 141 complete paired units we observed baseline_acceptance = 135/141 (0.9574468085106383) and guarded_acceptance = 141/141 (1.0), giving a paired difference of 0.04255319148936165 (exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125) with a 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Diagnostics associate the six discordant pairs with sanitizer normalization and single permitted repairs that enabled acceptance. Importantly, improved validator acceptance under the archived formal estimand does not by itself demonstrate reduced attacker success; attacker-centric evaluation requires an independent semantic-safety oracle. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, couple validator acceptance to semantic-safety oracles, diversify models and validators, and fix explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numeric claims above are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts (execution manifest [14]).

Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
